architecture:
GOAL: one streamlined production line on a single shop-floor host. It reuses the existing research engine unchanged and adds a recipe-guided, operator-assist measurement layer. Flow: onboarding (SKU + CAD + PDF drawing + manual bend ORDER) produces an immutable, versioned PartRecipe that is also registered as a benchmark reference. A hotfolder receives the ZEISS PLY, matches SKU to recipe, and enqueues a durable job. The engine worker runs; a postprocess step produces per-bend expected vs actual values (flange A/B length first, then angle and bend-line position) with honest states. A 16:9 kiosk shows the live 3D view, and a PDF report is produced per scan.

1. PROCESSES
- sherman-qc-api: `python -m apps.production_line.server` (C11). It runs uvicorn with exactly 1 worker over the existing app object from apps/api/main.py. The new routers are appended to ALL_ROUTERS (apps/api/routes/__init__.py:8-41). They must go there because the SPA catch-all registered at apps/api/main.py:45-59 shadows any GET route added after create_app(). The server adds RoutePolicyMiddleware (C04) plus request-id JSON access logs that redact `token=`. It keeps no job state in memory.
- sherman-qc-line: `python -m apps.production_line.service_main` (C11). It runs one HotfolderPoller per station plus one JobRunner (concurrency 1, matching the AGENTS.md one-heavy-run rule) plus heartbeats. Each inspect job spawns two subprocesses from a pinned engine bundle directory:
  (a) the existing worker backend/bend_analysis_worker.py, unchanged. It does shared registration, run_progressive_bend_inspection, enrichment, finalize_bend_report and artifacts (:143-299).
  (b) the new postprocess CLI (C06). It does validity gates, recipe binding, recipe-guided OML measurement, ShopfloorInspectionResultV1, viewer assets and the PDF.
  The supervisor (C02) enforces a wall-clock timeout, kills the process group and applies an RSS ceiling. The legacy launcher has none of these: it blocks on proc.wait() at backend/_server_legacy_impl.py:998.
- Kiosk: Chromium or Edge in --kiosk mode on the 16:9 screen at /station/<station_id>. It authenticates with a revocable station device token and polls GET /api/line/stations/<id>/latest every 2 s with an ETag. SSE is an optional accelerator.
- ZEISS cell PC (external): exports PLY/STL into an SMB share that is mounted as the station inbox. ZEISS has no "RoboScan 7000". Treat the source as a generic ZEISS INSPECT mesh export until the owner confirms the model, filename template and completion signal.
- Back office: the same SPA hosts /production/parts and the onboarding wizard (C09). The existing Vendor Setup page is reused for candidate review and bend ORDER tagging (apps/api/services/vendor_setup_service.py:89-204).

2. STORAGE
- Line data root, SHERMAN_LINE_DATA_ROOT: absolute and outside the git repo. It is refused if it resolves under data/, output/, outputs/, artifacts/, uploads/ or live_scans/. Contents:
  - db/line.sqlite3: scan_files, jobs + leases, events, heartbeats; WAL.
  - db/recipes.sqlite3: immutable part_recipes, sku_registry, release_drafts, recipe_expectations, benchmark_references.
  - db/security.sqlite3: device tokens.
  - recipes/cad/ and recipes/drawings/: content-addressed copies frozen at release.
  - archive/scans/YYYY/MM/<sha256><ext>, quarantine/YYYY-MM-DD/.
  - jobs/<job_id>/: workspaces.
  - engine/<bundle_id>/, logs/, secrets/ (0600 keys), backups/, config/.
- Line artifacts must never be written under the legacy OUTPUT_DIR. /api/aligned-scan/{job_id}.ply and /api/reference-mesh/{job_id}.ply serve any non-"bend_" job id without auth: apps/api/routes/jobs.py:20-21, the early return at apps/api/services/bend_inspection_service.py:92, and backend/_server_legacy_impl.py:1484-1517.
- Legacy state is unchanged and lives in the deployed app copy, never the dev repo:
  - catalog parts, bend specs and vendor drafts in data/qc_jobs.db (backend/part_catalog.py:31);
  - users in data/users.db (backend/auth.py:32);
  - CAD and drawings in uploads/parts_cad and uploads/parts_drawings (backend/_server_legacy_impl.py:3668,3831).
  The line reads them only at release time, through a CatalogPort (C05).
- Engine bundle (C04): an import-closure copy of the engine source with a sha256 manifest and an explicitly pinned runtime config. Running from the bundle removes two silent mutable inputs that the worker otherwise reads from the repo's output/:
  - output/improvement_loop/best_config.latest.json (backend/bend_inspection_pipeline.py:224-227);
  - output/unary_models/latest.json, a joblib pointer (domains/bend/services/structured_count_reporting_service.py:15, called at backend/bend_analysis_worker.py:227).
  Every job and result is stamped with engine_bundle_id.

3. DATA FLOW
A. Onboarding (C05 + C09). This closes the gap where the tagged order is write-only: analyze_from_catalog passes only cad_path, tolerance and a literal 0.5 (apps/api/services/bend_inspection_service.py:631-639).
  1. Create the part with a canonical SKU and enforce uniqueness.
  2. Upload CAD through the existing POST /api/parts/{id}/cad (native STEP candidates + CAS publish, backend/part_catalog.py:820-894).
  3. Upload the drawing through the existing POST /api/parts/{id}/drawing.
  4. In the existing Vendor Setup: confirm, remove or add marks, tag the bend ORDER, record operator confirmation.
  5. Fill the release draft: default and per-bend tolerances, and flange sides marked NOT_INSPECTED.
  6. POST release. It re-validates the draft: not stale (backend/part_catalog.py:915-935), order confirmed, every active mark confirmed, drawing attached, tolerances present. It builds PartRecipeV1 (stable bend_uids, included angles, sequence, machine moves), copies the CAD and drawing by sha256, and appends an immutable version that supersedes the previous one. It then registers the benchmark reference, emits RECIPE_RELEASED, and enqueues a recipe_expectations job. That job computes CAD-only OML nominal values, which the wizard shows back to the engineer.
B. Ingest (C02):
  1. Poll with os.scandir. No watchdog dependency, which keeps it safe on SMB.
  2. Ignore temp, dot and partial files. Optionally require a .done sidecar.
  3. A file is ready when size and mtime are unchanged for 3 polls, the minimum age has passed, and a read-open succeeds.
  4. Probe the PLY/STL header.
  5. Compute sha256 and archive the file atomically.
  6. Map filename to SKU with the longest-prefix rule.
  7. Resolve the active recipe. MATCHED: enqueue an inspect job, deduplicated by sha + recipe. Otherwise: write a quarantine record and reason file.
  Duplicates are idempotent, and a restart rescans the inbox.
C. Inspection (C02 runner + C06 postprocess + C03 geometry):
  1. Lease the job. Create the workspace with a frozen recipe.json. Check the recipe, CAD and scan hashes before spawning anything.
  2. Run the worker: registration including raw_scan_to_reference_transform, heatmap deviations, engine CAD bends and BEND_DECISION_CONTRACT_V1.
  3. Postprocess validity gates: abstention, fitness, RMSE, scale from the transform (UNIT_MISMATCH_SUSPECTED), frame consistency, recipe lines near the CAD mesh, surface coverage.
  4. Bind recipe bends to engine CAD bends (geometry + Hungarian + abstain). This is used only for observation states and cross-checks.
  5. Measure OML flange A/B lengths and the unfolded included angle with one algorithm on the CAD tessellation (expected) and on the full-resolution registered scan (actual), with support and edge-coverage gates.
  6. Apply the tolerance policy and write ShopfloorInspectionResultV1.
  7. Write decimated, index-aligned viewer assets, then the PDF.
  8. Complete the job with a summary and emit events.
D. Live UI (C07 + C08): the station feed supplies latest completed, active job, latest issue and history.
  - 3D view: CAD mesh, scan points, signed-deviation heatmap with a matching ±band legend, numbered bend labels, orbit/zoom/pan, focus on a row or on the worst value.
  - Per-bend table, flange first: expected / actual / Δ / tolerance / status.
  - Summary banner and PDF download.
  NOT_MEASURED is neutral grey text and is never green or red.
E. Benchmark + Jev (C05 export, C12 evaluator/scorecard, C10 Jev):
  - Released recipes become per-bend reference rows.
  - Jobs can be registered as benchmark cases with metrology truth.
  - The synthetic scorecard measures engineering capability, runtime and peak RSS, and is labelled synthetic, not physical accuracy.
  - Jev exporters build coordinate- and identity-free candidate states, human-sourced labels and grouped splits, all offline. The harness is dry-run by default, and nothing in runtime imports research/jev.

4. HONESTY MODEL (AGENTS.md; roadmap docs/research/2026-09-07_production_generalization_roadmap.md:237-253)
- Execution status, inspection validity, observation (FORMED/UNFORMED/UNKNOWN) and per-quantity conformance are separate fields.
- authority is fixed to OPERATOR_ASSIST with production_disposition NOT_AUTHORIZED (contracts/ui/bend_results.py:114; docs/release/ENTERPRISE_BEND_PROMOTION_GATES.md:16).
- The engine's legacy PASS/FAIL/WARNING values are evidence only.
- Placeholder geometry (assignment_source CAD_LOCAL_NEIGHBORHOOD, backend/feature_detection/bend_detector.py:351-366) never becomes an actual value.
- Worker and postprocess failures are execution failures, never a part FAIL.
- Synthetic results go in the engineering ledger and are not unseen-family accuracy.

contracts:
All contracts live in contracts/production/ (C01). They are pydantic v2 models with ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True), and every model carries a literal `schema` tag. Wave-1 chunks that cannot import them (C02, C03, C04) duplicate the string literals below, and C11's tests/test_prod_contract_parity.py asserts the copies are equal.

0. CONVENTIONS
- Units are mm and degrees.
- Frame "reference_mesh_raw" means the CAD model coordinates as tessellated by load_cad_geometry (backend/bend_inspection_pipeline.py:428) and exported by the worker as reference_mesh.ply (backend/bend_analysis_worker.py:185). Recipe bend lines come from catalog part_bend_specs in the same model coordinates. They are checked against the mesh at runtime; if they do not sit on it, the result is RECIPE_FRAME_MISMATCH.
- Angles: every nominal, expected and actual angle is the INCLUDED angle between the two flanges (180 = flat; acute angles allowed).
  - Native STEP candidates store the sweep: target_angle is the mean sweep (backend/vendor_native_step_upload_v1.py:129-132). Convert with included = 180 − sweep.
  - The mesh detector folds its angle as 180 − arccos|n1·n2| (backend/feature_detection/bend_detector.py:1767-1771). It is used only as a cross-check.
- Flange length v1 is OUTSIDE_MOLD_LINE (OML): for bend b and side S, the distance from the OML virtual sharp (the intersection of the two fitted outer-surface planes) to the far boundary of S.
  - It is measured inside the outer plane of S, perpendicular to the bend direction, within the bend's axial corridor.
  - Far boundary kinds:
    - FREE_EDGE: estimated as the median over axial bins of the per-bin maximum perpendicular extent, after radius-outlier removal.
    - ADJACENT_BEND: the distance to the parallel OML sharp of the neighbouring bend.
  - Expected and actual use the identical algorithm, on the CAD tessellation and on the registered scan respectively.
- Side naming: side A is the flange whose in-plane outward unit vector has the larger dot product with +X. Ties (|Δ| < 1e-6) are broken by +Y, then +Z.
- Canonical JSON: UTF-8, sort_keys, separators (",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False. Floats are normalised with round(x, 6), and -0.0 becomes 0.0. Hashes are sha256 hex over those bytes.
- IDs:
  - recipe_id = "<SKU>@v<version>"
  - job_id = "line_" + 32 hex characters (uuid4)
  - scan_file_id = "scan_" + sha256[:24]
  - bend_uid = "bu_" + sha256("<cad_sha256>|<source>|<canonical sorted endpoints rounded to 1e-3>|<radius rounded to 1e-3 or none>")[:20]
  - event id = SQLite autoincrement integer

1. SKU (domains/production/recipe/sku.py)
- canonical_sku: NFKC normalise, strip, replace internal whitespace runs with "-", uppercase ASCII letters. Allowed charset is [A-Z0-9._-], length 1-64, and the first character must be [A-Z0-9]. Anything else raises SKU_INVALID. Uniqueness is enforced on the canonical form.
- parse_scan_filename(filename, known_skus, pattern=None) returns {status OK|UNPARSEABLE|UNMATCHED|AMBIGUOUS, sku, serial, scan_timestamp (ISO or null), remainder}.
  1. Strip the directory and one .ply/.stl extension, case-insensitively.
  2. Canonicalise the stem.
  3. Try an exact match.
  4. Otherwise take the longest known SKU that is a prefix of the stem and is followed by "_", "-" or ".".
  5. In the remainder, a token matching \d{8}[T_-]?\d{4,6} is the timestamp, and the first other token is the serial.
  - Two equal-length competing matches give AMBIGUOUS.
  - An optional regex (SHERMAN_LINE_FILENAME_REGEX) must contain a named group "sku" and replaces the prefix rule.
  - Never guess.

6. STEP CLI CONTRACTS
All steps are launched by the runner with cwd=<engine_root> and PYTHONPATH=<engine_root>:<engine_root>/backend. The environment carries the thread caps (OMP_NUM_THREADS, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS, MKL_NUM_THREADS, NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS, VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS), as legacy sets them at backend/_server_legacy_impl.py:937-948. It also carries BEND_INSPECTION_CONFIG = the bundled config or <engine_root>/config/NONE, and SHERMAN_QC_F1_PROGRAM_STATUS_PATH = the settings value, which is fail-closed when missing.
a) Worker (existing, unchanged):
   <python> <worker_script> --job-id <job_id> --cad-path <abs cad> --scan-path <abs scan> --part-id <sku> --part-name <part_name|sku> --tolerance-angle <max(default angle plus, minus)> --tolerance-radius <max(default flange plus, minus)> --output-dir <ws>/engine
   - Stdout is tab-separated "PROGRESS\t{json}", "RESULT\t{json}" or "ERROR\t{json}" (backend/bend_analysis_worker.py:84-85).
   - Success is exit 0 plus a RESULT line.
b) Postprocess (C06), inspect mode:
   <python> -m domains.production.inspection.postprocess_cli --mode inspect --job-id <id> --station-id <sid> --engine-bundle-id <bid> --recipe <ws>/recipe.json --scan <abs scan> --engine-dir <ws>/engine --out <ws>/result
   CAD-expectations mode:
   --mode cad-expectations --recipe <path> --cad <abs cad> --out <ws>/result
   - Uses the same stdout protocol.
   - Exit 0: success.
   - Exit 2: invalid input; result/postprocess_error.json {code, message} is written.
   - Exit 3: internal error.
   - The PDF is rendered inside postprocess. If rendering fails, artifacts.pdf is null and a warning is added, but the exit code is still 0.
   - Re-render: python -m domains.production.reporting.render_cli --result <json> --job-dir <ws> --out <pdf>.

7. ShopfloorInspectionResultV1 (schema "sherman_shopfloor_inspection_result_v1")
Top-level fields:
- job_id, station_id, created_at, sku, part_name
- recipe {recipe_id, version, recipe_sha256}
- scan {file_name, sha256, serial?, scan_timestamp?, received_at}
- engine {bundle_id, worker_report_sha256, algorithm_versions {binding "recipe_binding_v1", measurement "oml_flange_v1", viewer "viewer_assets_v1"}}
- authority {mode "OPERATOR_ASSIST", production_disposition "NOT_AUTHORIZED", note}: literals
- inspection_validity {state VALID|INSUFFICIENT_CAPTURE|UNTRUSTED_REGISTRATION|UNIT_MISMATCH_SUSPECTED|UNSUPPORTED_INPUT, reasons[], metrology_qualified false, registration {fitness, rmse_mm, scale, abstained, frame "reference_mesh_raw"}, coverage {surface_coverage_ratio?}}
- summary {state ALL_MEASURED_IN_TOLERANCE|OUT_OF_TOLERANCE_FOUND|INCOMPLETE|INVALID_INSPECTION, bends_total, quantities_required, quantities_in_tolerance, quantities_out_of_tolerance, quantities_not_measured, worst {bend_uid, quantity, deviation, tolerance_plus, tolerance_minus, margin_ratio}?, reasons[]}
- sequence_check {state CONSISTENT|OUT_OF_ORDER_SUSPECTED|NOT_EVALUATED, detail}
- bends [BendRowV1, sorted by sequence_index]
- extra_engine_bends [{engine_bend_id, reason}]
- viewer_assets {reference_mesh?, scan?, deviations?, deviation_count?, deviation_sign "SIGNED_ALONG_CAD_NORMAL", frame "reference_mesh_raw", heatmap_band_mm, heatmap_unavailable_reason?}
- artifacts {pdf?, overview_png?}
- warnings[]

BendRowV1:
- bend_uid, label, sequence_index, machine_move_index?
- binding {state BOUND|UNBOUND|AMBIGUOUS, engine_bend_id?, reasons}
- observation {state FORMED|UNFORMED|UNKNOWN, detail, reasons}: taken from the engine decision_contract row of the bound engine bend (finalize_bend_report.py:130-150). UNBOUND or AMBIGUOUS gives UNKNOWN.
- quantities [QuantityResultV1] in a fixed order: FLANGE_A_LENGTH, FLANGE_B_LENGTH, ANGLE, BEND_LINE_POSITION, then optionally BEND_LINE_LENGTH and INNER_RADIUS
- display {line_start_mm, line_end_mm, label_anchor_mm, side_a_anchor_mm?, side_b_anchor_mm?}
- evidence {engine {status_legacy, measured_angle_folded_deg, assignment_source, expected_edge_distance_mm, measured_edge_distance_mm}?, notes[]}

QuantityResultV1:
- quantity, unit mm|deg, required
- expected?, expected_source (CAD_OML_V1|CAD_PLANES_V1|ENGINE_REPORT)
- actual?, actual_method (SCAN_OML_OUTER_FIT_V1|SCAN_OML_INNER_FIT_PLUS_CAD_THICKNESS_V1|SCAN_PLANES_V1|ENGINE_REPORT)
- deviation? (= actual − expected)
- tolerance {plus, minus, source}?
- conformance IN_TOLERANCE|OUT_OF_TOLERANCE|NOT_MEASURED|NOT_APPLICABLE
- reason? One of: INVALID_INSPECTION, INSUFFICIENT_SUPPORT, EDGE_NOT_OBSERVED, PLANE_FIT_UNSTABLE, DEGENERATE_ANGLE, FAR_BOUNDARY_AMBIGUOUS, ADJACENT_BEND_NOT_MEASURED, NOMINAL_UNAVAILABLE, METHOD_DISAGREEMENT, PLACEHOLDER_GEOMETRY, NO_TOLERANCE, BEND_NOT_FORMED, NOT_INSPECTED_BY_RECIPE
- boundary_kind FREE_EDGE|ADJACENT_BEND?
- margin_ratio? (= |dev| / tolerance)
- evidence {support_points, edge_coverage_ratio, plane_rms_mm}

Required quantities:
- FLANGE_A_LENGTH and FLANGE_B_LENGTH, except when the side is NOT_INSPECTED or the bend is BEND_NOT_FORMED, which makes them NOT_APPLICABLE.
- ANGLE.
- BEND_LINE_POSITION only when a tolerance exists.

derive_summary, a pure function mirrored in frontend stationView.ts:
- validity ≠ VALID → INVALID_INSPECTION
- else any required OUT_OF_TOLERANCE → OUT_OF_TOLERANCE_FOUND
- else any required NOT_MEASURED → INCOMPLETE
- else ALL_MEASURED_IN_TOLERANCE
Validators reject:
- IN or OUT without expected, actual, deviation and tolerance
- NOT_MEASURED that carries an actual value or has no reason
- any IN or OUT while validity ≠ VALID
- summary.state ≠ derive_summary
- inconsistent counts
- altered authority literals
- rows that are unsorted or duplicated

8. LineEventV1 (schema "sherman_line_event_v1")
Fields: id, ts, kind, station_id?, job_id?, scan_file_id?, principal {kind, id, role}?, payload.
Kinds: SCAN_RECEIVED, SCAN_DUPLICATE, SCAN_QUARANTINED, JOB_QUEUED, JOB_STARTED, JOB_PROGRESS (at most 1 per second per job), JOB_COMPLETED, JOB_FAILED, JOB_CANCELLED, JOB_RECOVERED, JOB_RETRY_REQUESTED, JOB_CANCEL_REQUESTED, QUARANTINE_ASSIGNED, QUARANTINE_DISMISSED, RECIPE_RELEASED, RECIPE_RETIRED, EXPECTATIONS_READY, DEVICE_TOKEN_ISSUED, DEVICE_TOKEN_REVOKED.

9. HTTP API
Capabilities:
- line.read: users with role viewer, operator or admin; or a device token scoped to its own station.
- line.operate: operator or admin.
- parts.write: operator or admin.
- parts.delete and parts.import: admin.
- recipe.release: SHERMAN_RELEASE_ROLES, default "admin".
- devices.manage and metrics.read: admin.
If the line is not configured, these routes return 503.

/api/production (C05):
- GET /parts
- POST /parts
- GET /parts/{part_id}/onboarding
- GET|PUT /parts/{part_id}/release-draft
- POST /parts/{part_id}/recipe/release: 201 released, 200 unchanged, 422 {detail: {codes, messages}}, 409 {detail: {codes}}
- GET /recipes/by-sku/{sku}
- GET /recipes/{recipe_id}
- GET /recipes/{recipe_id}/expectations: {status PENDING|READY|FAILED, algo_version, expectations?, job_id?}

/api/line (C07):
- GET /jobs?station_id&status&sku&limit&before
- GET /jobs/{id}
- GET /jobs/{id}/result
- GET /jobs/{id}/artifacts/{name}
- POST /jobs/{id}/retry

- POST /stream-token: 300 s

- GET /quarantine

- POST /quarantine/{scan_file_id}/dismiss
- GET /status
- GET /health/ready: no auth, minimal body {ready, checks}, 503 when not ready
- POST|GET /devices, DELETE /devices/{token_id}
- GET /metrics: Prometheus text

StationFeedV1 (schema "sherman_station_feed_v1"):
- station_id, etag, server_time
- latest_completed {job: LineJobSummary, result: ShopfloorInspectionResultV1, artifacts {name: url}}?
- active {job}?
- latest_issue {kind QUARANTINE|JOB_FAILED, at, file_name?, reason_code, message}?
- recent [LineJobSummary, at most 10]
LineJobSummary = {job_id, kind, station_id, sku, part_name, recipe_id, recipe_version, scan_file_name, serial, execution_status, stage, progress, created_at, started_at, finished_at, failure_code, summary_state, inspection_validity}.
Artifact URL = /api/line/jobs/{job_id}/artifacts/{name}.

10. REPORT (PDF): rendered only from ShopfloorInspectionResultV1, plus the overview PNG when one exists.
- Page 1:
  - header: SKU, part name, revision, recipe vN + sha8, scan file + sha8, serial, station, scan time, engine bundle id
  - summary banner with counts
  - operator-assist disclaimer
  - registration/validity box
  - overview image
- Following pages: a table in sequence order with columns Seq | Bend | Move | Flange A exp/act/Δ/tol/status | Flange B … | Angle … | Bend-line pos Δ | Observation | Notes.

11. JEV DATASET (research/jev)

1) store/line_store.py: LineStore(db_path, clock=utc_now).

    - jobs: LineJobV1 columns; partial UNIQUE index on dedupe_key; index on (execution_status, priority DESC, created_at).

3) ingest/ply_probe.py: probe(path) -> ProbeResult{ok, fmt, vertex_count, face_count, header_bytes, expected_min_bytes, bbox_mm|None, reason}.
  - PLY ascii, binary_little_endian and binary_big_endian: any scalar vertex properties; face list properties.
  - Binary STL: size must equal 84 + 50n exactly. ASCII STL: 'solid' header plus a streamed facet count.
  - Binary PLY is PLY_TRUNCATED if size < header + vertex_count × stride (+ 13 × faces minimum for triangle lists). Zero vertices is EMPTY_SCAN. Anything else unrecognised is PLY_HEADER_INVALID or UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT.
  - bbox uses a numpy memmap of x,y,z, only when vertex_count ≤ 20M. Never read a whole file into Python memory.
4) ingest/hotfolder.py:
  - HotfolderConfig(station_id, inbox, archive_root, quarantine_root, poll_interval_s=1.0, stable_polls=3, min_age_s=2.0, min_size_bytes=1024, extensions=('.ply', '.stl'), sidecar_mode='off'|'required', source_policy='move'|'copy_leave', recursive=False, unstable_timeout_s=1800).

3) cad_flanges.py: expect_bends(mesh, bends, params) -> list[CadBendExpectation]. Per bend:
  - Candidate planar patches have |n·d| < sin 2° and lie within inner_radius + thickness + 3 mm of the bend line inside the axial corridor. The corridor is the bend line's projected span trimmed by min(2 mm, 5% of the span).
  - Split the patches into two sides. On each side the two parallel planes are outer and inner: outer is the plane farther from the other side's centroid. Thickness = plane separation.
  - OML sharp = intersection of the two outer planes. u = the in-plane unit vector ⟂ d that points into the flange. tangent_offset = where the planar patch starts.
  - Side A/B naming per CONTRACTS §0.
  - Far boundary:
    - FREE_EDGE when the side's planar region inside the corridor ends at a free boundary. Expected length uses the same per-bin-max estimator as the scan (below), applied to the exact CAD vertices plus deterministic dense surface samples.
    - ADJACENT_BEND when it ends at another bend that is parallel within 2°: the distance between the two sharps.
    - Otherwise FAR_BOUNDARY_AMBIGUOUS. A non-straight edge (per-bin extent range > 0.5 mm) is NOMINAL_UNAVAILABLE.
  - Included angle = 180 − the angle between the outer planes' outward normals, oriented away from the material. Never folded.
  - check_bend_lines_near_mesh(mesh, bends) -> the fraction of bends within inner_radius + thickness + 2 mm of the surface.
4) flange_length.py: measure_cad(mesh, expectations) and measure_scan(expectations, points_ref, params) both return list[ScanBendMeasurement] from the shared core. Per side:
  1. Crop to the corridor: axial span ± margin; laterally from tangent_offset + 1 mm out to the CAD length + max(10 mm, 10%) along u; within 5 mm of the CAD outer or inner plane. Only points whose nearest CAD triangle belongs to that side's planar patches are used, so arc points are excluded.
  2. Fit planes robustly (IRLS Tukey, ≤ 5 iterations) separately near the CAD outer and inner planes. Re-associate points within max(0.3 mm, 3σ) of the fitted plane.
  3. Method:
    - OUTER_FIT when outer support ≥ min_side_support_points and ≥ 40% of the corridor area bins are occupied.
    - Otherwise INNER_FIT_PLUS_CAD_THICKNESS: offset by the CAD thickness, flagged.
    - Otherwise INSUFFICIENT_SUPPORT.
  4. rms > 0.5 → PLANE_FIT_UNSTABLE. Outer planes less than 5° apart → DEGENERATE_ANGLE.
  5. Scan sharp = intersection of the fitted outer planes.
  6. FREE_EDGE edge estimate = the median over axial bins (max(5, span/5 mm) bins) of the per-bin maximum projection along u, measured from the sharp, after radius-outlier removal (≥ 3 neighbours within max(0.5 mm, 2·spacing)). Edge coverage = the fraction of bins whose maximum lies within max(0.5 mm, 2·spacing + 3σ) of the median. Below min_edge_coverage → EDGE_NOT_OBSERVED.
  7. ADJACENT_BEND = the distance between the two scan sharps at mid-span; if the neighbour failed, ADJACENT_BEND_NOT_MEASURED.
  - The actual included angle comes from the fitted outer normals, oriented to agree with the CAD.
  - Use cKDTree on CAD samples with seeded sampling. Performance target: 2M points × 8 bends ≤ 30 s single-threaded.
5) angles.py: sweep_to_included, included_to_sweep, folded_candidates(folded) -> (a, 180 − a), angle_between(n1, n2).
6) binding.py: bind(recipe_bends, engine_bends, gates) -> BindingResult.

  - Ties are broken deterministically by id. Report extra engine bends.

  - surface_coverage(points_ref, mesh, spacing) = the fraction of CAD samples with a scan point within max(1 mm, 2·spacing).

RULES:

- Custody: do NOT open any sibling file under research/ (it holds authorization and one-shot artifacts), data/, output/, artifacts/ or uploads/. Tests use synthetic records only.

- The owner asked to install the TypeSafe skill (`claude plugin marketplace add typesafe-ai/skills` then `claude plugin install typesafe@typesafe-ai`). The orchestrator should do that, and you should load the skill before coding the client if it is present. Otherwise follow the docs as verified on 2026-10-17:
  - POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone with Authorization: Bearer.
  - Body {state, model, questions: {id: {type 'noul'|'choice'|'score', instructions, criteria}}}.
  - Response {model (versioned id), answers {id: noul | choice+probabilities+confidence | score+legend+probabilities+confidence}, usage}.
  - Limits: 32 MiB, nesting ≤ 64, finite numbers, UTF-8 without BOM, choice ≤ 255, score 2-10 levels, 64k tokens per request, 32k per question.
  - 400/401/413/415/422 fail fast; 429/529 use exponential backoff.
  - jev-latest → jev-1.13.0 and jev-preview → jev-1.14.0. Jev is not fine-tuned on customer data and is text-only.
- The API key the owner pasted in chat must NEVER appear in any file, test, log, fixture or commit. Read TYPESAFE_API_KEY from the environment at live run time only.
- PYT := env PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 PYTHONPATH=.:backend OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -c /dev/null --noconftest -p no:cacheprovider.

FAMILIES:
(A) CAD_ONBOARDING_CANDIDATE: every CAD candidate of a released recipe, both active bends and removed_candidates.
  - Features, from the recipe and expectations only: bend-line length, nominal included and sweep angle and their source, nominal radius, thickness, side boundary kinds and status, extent_semantics, and the part's candidate count (allowed, ablated).
  - Labels:
    - active and review-confirmed → 1, operator_confirmed;
    - removed with issue not_a_bend → 0, operator_removed_not_a_bend;
    - removed with issue wrong_location → null (a real bend with wrong geometry);
    - manual 'missing' marks → recall-accounting rows with no state.
(B) SCAN_ENGINE_CANDIDATE: every engine match and unmatched detection in a line job workspace (engine/bend_inspection_report.json).
  - Identity-free scalars: folded measured angle and both unfold candidates, radius, line length, confidence, flange areas, observability/visibility/local_support/side_balance scores, assignment kind.
  - CAD-assisted relations (direction/offset deltas to the nearest recipe bend), flagged so a CAD-free ablation can drop them.
  - Labels:
    - Human marker reviews: real_bend → 1, not_bend_outline → 0, uncertain → null. Only when they are explicitly supplied and their coordinate_frame is reference_mesh_raw.
    - recipe_binding_weak: bound + FORMED + measured → weak 1; an unbound detection more than 10 mm from every recipe bend → weak 0. Kept in a separate column and never used as evaluation truth.
  - The pipeline's observability_state is a feature, never a label.

MODULES:
1) state_v1.py: build_state(record).
  - Recursive deny-list: the INFERENCE_FORBIDDEN_KEYS semantics, plus anchors, line_start/line_end, any 3-vector coordinates, ids, sku, part, job, recipe, scan, file, timestamp, serial and station.
  - Finite numbers rounded to 4 significant digits. NaN becomes null plus '<key>_missing': true.
  - Unit-suffixed keys; depth ≤ 8.
  - record_id = sha256(source sha + candidate key)[:24], kept outside the state.
2) questions_v1.py: QUESTION_SET_V1 (is_real_bend as noul with true/false criteria; candidate_kind as choice over bend, flange_edge, cut_edge, hole_wall, emboss, noise, other; evidence_quality as a 4-level score) and question_set_sha256. A 'verbalized_v1' variant is hashed separately.
3) request_v1.py: build_request(state, model) and validate_request(body). Enforce the limits above with a conservative token estimate of len(json)/3.
4) client_v1.py:
  - Dry run is the default. It writes requests/<record_id>.json and a summary {count, est_tokens, est_cost_usd at $0.042 per million input tokens}.
  - Live needs both --live and TYPESAFE_API_KEY, else exit 2.
  - Versioned model ids only; aliases are rejected unless --allow-alias.
  - 10 s timeout. Honour Retry-After on 429/529. Fail fast on other 4xx.
  - Cache responses by sha256(body). answers.jsonl stores the response model and usage.
  - Send only dev and calib records; eval only with --include-eval.
5) labels_v1.py and splits_v1.py:
  - labels.jsonl is a sidecar.
  - Splits come from an explicit manifest {sku_family → dev|calib|eval|excluded} plus {sku → family}.
  - Families flagged holdout, sealed or one-shot → excluded. No family spans two splits. Split ids never appear in the state.
6) export_onboarding_v1.py and export_scan_candidates_v1.py:
  - Inputs only from explicit paths: C05 export_benchmark JSONL or recipe JSON files, and job workspaces under an explicit --jobs-root.
  - Refuse inputs under the repo's data/, output/, outputs/, artifacts/, uploads/ or live_scans/ unless --authorization FILE is given; record that file's sha in the manifest.
  - Write states.jsonl, labels.jsonl and manifest.json atomically into a new --out dir; refuse an existing one.
7) evaluate_v1.py:
  - Join answers and labels.
  - Metrics: AUC, Brier, log-loss, ECE(10), precision and recall at a threshold frozen on dev/calib (operating_point.json with its sha). An abstention band maps to 'review'.
  - Baselines: engine confidence where present, and sklearn LogisticRegression on the numeric state fields with the identical split.
  - Recall-preserving pruning rate at dev recall ≥ 0.99, with group-bootstrap CIs. Worst-family recall.
  - Flag any consumed or retrospective source as 'exploratory_not_unseen'.
8) cli.py: `python -m research.jev.cli export-onboarding|export-scan|dry-run|live|evaluate ...`.
9) docs/research/JEV_BEND_CANDIDATE_DATASET_V1.md covers: purpose, families, schema, label sources and weights, splits, custody, and egress policy (owner approval + ZDR/enterprise terms before any live call). It gives the run commands and states explicitly that Jev output is not wired into runtime decisions.
